stem: A monitoring team wants to run a custom, stateful, windowed aggregation over a live event stream, computing a rolling five-minute average per device using SQL logic they will maintain over time.

choices.text: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
Amazon Data Firehose delivering to Amazon S3
Amazon MSK broker cluster running alone
A scheduled AWS Glue ETL job

rationale: Managed Service for Apache Flink is the managed runtime built for custom, windowed, stateful stream computation in SQL, Java, Python, or Scala, matching a rolling five-minute average the team maintains itself. Data Firehose only buffers and delivers records toward a configured destination, with no windowed-aggregation logic of its own. MSK is the Kafka-compatible transport that carries the stream; it needs a separate processing layer to compute anything over the data. A scheduled Glue ETL job processes data in batch runs; it does not perform continuous, low-latency computation over a live, still-arriving stream.
